open_points.subject: A2: Accepted decision A2 — What reaches the Portal store
open_points.text:
A source it cannot open as one of them fails with the
   UNREADABLE_IMAGE member of = models.PlacementFailure, whatever dimensions its header declares. For a source
   it opens, checks run in this order: a first frame whose width times height is above the imported
   `MAX_PIXELS` constant fails with the TOO_MANY_PIXELS member, a source that cannot be decoded with the
   UNREADABLE_IMAGE member, and a result longer than the imported `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` constant, the Portal's
   read limit, with the TOO_LARGE member.
open_points.question: Which failure applies when the library opens the image and decoding succeeds, but a later preparation or JPEG-encoding operation raises an error before an output result exists?
options: Treat every preparation or encoding error as UNREADABLE_IMAGE.
Treat an encoding or output-construction error as A3 condition 5 and return UNREADABLE_FILE.
Define separate mappings for each ImageOps.exif_transpose, convert, thumbnail, composite and save failure.
open_points.default_guess: Treat failures before successful JPEG bytes exist as UNREADABLE_IMAGE unless the binary-store write itself fails.

witness.initial: A source has an allowed signature, opens, has dimensions below MAX_PIXELS and decodes its first frame, but Image.save raises while encoding the prepared JPEG.
events: The deliverer opens and decodes the source.
The image library raises during JPEG encoding before any store write.
outcomes: The delivery fails with UNREADABLE_IMAGE because no decodable-and-preparable result was produced.
The delivery reaches A3 condition 5 and fails with UNREADABLE_FILE because creation of the stored image failed.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees a different PlacementFailure.

open_points.subject: A2: Accepted decision A2 — What reaches the Portal store
open_points.text:
A source it cannot open as one of them fails with the
   UNREADABLE_IMAGE member of = models.PlacementFailure, whatever dimensions its header declares. For a source
   it opens, checks run in this order: a first frame whose width times height is above the imported
   `MAX_PIXELS` constant fails with the TOO_MANY_PIXELS member, a source that cannot be decoded with the
   UNREADABLE_IMAGE member
open_points.question: What exact image-library operation constitutes opening, what operation proves that the first frame can be decoded, and must library decompression-bomb limits or warnings be disabled so that MAX_PIXELS alone decides the stated precedence?
options: Image.open is opening; read size immediately; a later load of frame zero proves decoding; configure the library so only MAX_PIXELS enforces the pixel limit.
Opening includes loading frame zero, so any error raised before loading finishes is UNREADABLE_IMAGE.
Use the library's own decompression-bomb policy and map its rejection to TOO_MANY_PIXELS.
open_points.default_guess: Use Image.open as opening, inspect its size before a forced load of frame zero, and disable or override the library's independent pixel-limit policy.

witness.initial: An allowed-signature image has a header declaring more than MAX_PIXELS and compressed data that would fail when frame zero is loaded; the pinned library can inspect the header lazily.
events: One implementation reads the dimensions immediately after Image.open.
Another implementation treats opening as successful only after forcing frame-zero decoding.
outcomes: The first implementation returns TOO_MANY_PIXELS without decoding the pixels.
The second implementation returns UNREADABLE_IMAGE when the forced decode fails.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees a different PlacementFailure for the same bytes.

open_points.subject: A1: Accepted decision A1 — What a file of the folder becomes
open_points.text: INV-01: after a scan, a placement, a repeated placement and a mark, the source folder holds the same files with the same bytes, modification times and modes (`test_no_operation_changes_the_source_folder`).
open_points.question: Must the required test also show that subfolders, symbolic links, other non-file entries, directory metadata and link metadata are unchanged, so that it demonstrates that no operation changes anything in the source folder as INV-01 requires?
options: Compare the complete source tree, including every entry type and relevant metadata.
Limit INV-01 to regular files and rewrite the invariant accordingly.
Keep the stated test and treat unmentioned entry types and directory metadata as unchecked.
open_points.default_guess: Compare the complete tree and its relevant metadata before and after all four operations.

witness.initial: The source folder contains a regular photo and an otherwise unused subfolder.
events: An implementation changes the unused subfolder's mode or modification time but leaves every regular file unchanged.
outcomes: The described required test passes because the same files, bytes, file modification times and file modes remain.
INV-01 fails because an operation changed something in the source folder.
witness.observer: The owner or Syncthing sees the changed subfolder metadata.

open_points.subject: A1: Accepted decision A1 — What a file of the folder becomes
open_points.text: INV-02: for content with no placement, an empty or absolute name, a name with an empty, `.` or `..` segment, an ignored name at any level, a folder, and a path through a symbolic link each fail with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure and add no file except the project lock, and a trace of every file the process opens while the delivery runs shows no opening of the named file, of a folder past the segment that fails or of a link's target (`test_a_name_a_scan_would_not_report_is_not_delivered`).
open_points.question: What must show INV-02 for the condition-1 cases this item does not name, including an absent last segment, an unreadable metadata operation, a non-link folder-opening failure and a last segment that is a non-regular object other than a folder?
options: Add each remaining condition-1 branch to the traced-open test.
State that the listed cases are an exhaustive equivalence partition and identify which listed case covers each remaining branch.
Narrow INV-02 to only the cases listed by the required test.
open_points.default_guess: Add traced-open cases for every distinct condition-1 refusal branch.

open_points.subject: A3: Accepted decision A3 — One placement per project and content
open_points.text: INV-06: a second placement returns the first publication and leaves every stored image and placement record unchanged, with one placement record in place (`test_a_repeated_placement_writes_no_durable_state`).
open_points.question: How must the Required tests demonstrate the 'at most one placement' part of INV-06 when two first deliveries for the same project and source content overlap?
options: Run concurrent first deliveries and assert one placement identity, one record and no duplicate stored image.
State a storage uniqueness or locking check that the test exercises directly.
Restrict the invariant to sequential deliveries.
open_points.default_guess: Test two synchronized concurrent first deliveries and assert that exactly one durable placement and its one stored image result.

witness.initial: No placement exists for a project and source_id.
events: Caller A starts delivery and passes the existing-placement check.
Caller B starts the same delivery before A writes the placement record.
outcomes: A locking or uniqueness implementation creates one placement and the other call replays it.
An implementation satisfying only the sequential test creates two stored images or two records.
witness.observer: The calling flows or a later scan sees duplicate or inconsistent durable state.

open_points.subject: A3: Accepted decision A3 — One placement per project and content
open_points.text: leaves every stored image and placement record unchanged
open_points.question: Must the Required test also assert that publication marks and every other durable store remain byte-for-byte unchanged, as the invariant and rule 2 say the repeated placement 'writes nothing'?
options: Assert no write calls and no changes in any durable store, including publication marks.
Limit 'writes nothing' to stored images and placement records.
Permit idempotent rewrites whose final values are unchanged.
open_points.default_guess: Assert that no durable backend write is invoked, including no rewrite of a publication mark.

witness.initial: A placement already has a publication mark.
events: The implementation rewrites the existing mark with identical values while leaving images and placement records unchanged.
outcomes: The described test passes because its named durable objects are unchanged.
INV-06 fails because the repeated placement performed a durable write.
witness.observer: A storage audit, write counter or failure-injection backend sees the extra write.

open_points.subject: A3: Accepted decision A3 — One placement per project and content
open_points.text: INV-07: a replaced file is reported as a new `ready` photo while the earlier image and mark stay (`test_a_replaced_file_is_a_new_photo_and_the_first_delivery_stays`), and a removed file keeps its delivery (`test_removing_a_file_keeps_its_delivery`).
open_points.question: What exact assertions must show that the earlier placement record, stored image and publication mark all remain unchanged in both the replacement and removal histories required by INV-07?
options: For both histories, compare all three durable artifacts before and after.
Define 'keeps its delivery' explicitly as keeping those three artifacts unchanged.
Reduce INV-07 to only the artifacts expressly asserted in each test description.
open_points.default_guess: Snapshot and compare the placement record, stored image and mark in both histories.

open_points.subject: A3: Accepted decision A3 — One placement per project and content
open_points.text: INV-19: delivering content that has no placement under the name of a conflict copy fails with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure, adds no file except the project lock and changes no existing file (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`).
open_points.question: What must the Required test observe to prove that the conflict copy was never read, rather than merely proving that reading it produced no placement?
options: Trace file opens and reads and assert that the conflict-copy last segment is never opened for reading.
Use a file object that records or fails any read attempt.
Change INV-19 from 'never reads' to only 'never places'.
open_points.default_guess: Trace opens and reads and assert that the conflict-copy file is never opened for reading.

witness.initial: A conflict-copy file has content with no existing placement.
events: The calling flow requests delivery using its conflict-copy name.
An implementation opens and reads the whole file, then notices the ignored mark and returns NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT without writing anything.
outcomes: The described Required test passes because the refusal and durable state are correct.
INV-19 fails because the new-placement attempt read the conflict copy.
witness.observer: A file-access trace or access-control monitor sees the read.

open_points.subject: A7: Accepted decision A7 — Time
open_points.text: INV-13: a counting clock is read once by a mark and not at all by a scan, a delivery or the health answer (`test_only_the_mark_reads_the_clock`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
open_points.question: Which mark histories must be exercised to show the at-most-once invariant and rule 2's exact reading behavior for refusal before the clock point, refusal after it, a replayed mark and a publication conflict?
options: Test each pre-clock and post-clock exit and assert respectively zero or exactly one reading.
State an exhaustive control-flow check that proves every mark path crosses the clock read at most once and at the required point.
Require the clock count only for a successful first mark.
open_points.default_guess: Test every distinct mark exit: pre-validation refusals read zero; successful, post-clock-refused, replayed and conflicting marks read exactly once.

witness.initial: A placement already has a mark for photo_id A.
events: The caller repeats the mark with photo_id A.
One implementation returns the stored mark before reading the clock.
Another follows rule 2 and reads the clock once before discovering the replay.
outcomes: The replay reads once and writes nothing.
witness.observer: A counting clock sees the difference, although the caller receives the same replayed mark.
